rationale: Extended the leader-admission case so the same run also shows whether the outsider's entries reach the node's log and FSM, and queued it as a fresh experiment because the harness bytes changed after the previous receipt. Local construction feedback showed the entry stored and applied; the retained receipt is what the account will rest on.

scope.description: The same single-node empty-configuration restart as the previous case, extended by one phase: after the outsider is accepted as leader, it sends one AppendEntries carrying a single command entry with a commit index covering it, and the probe records whether the entry is stored in the node's log and reaches its FSM.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own test facilities; snapshotting is disabled so the configuration is empty.
The outsider remains transport-reachable and its term is the node's current term at the time of the second request.
The entry is a plain command entry with no configuration semantics.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, apply five commands, restart the node with NewRaft on a fresh transport and emit the setup event; sleep six heartbeat timeouts and record state; send an outsider AppendEntries with term+1 and no entries, then send a second AppendEntries from the same outsider carrying one command entry with a leader commit index covering it; wait for the applied index to advance, scan the log store for the payload, and emit the outsider-entries event with the stored flag, the last index and the last applied index before and after.
experiment.requirement: A node that recovers its configuration from its own log must not store or apply entries sent by a server outside that configuration.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose requests are processed and processLogs decides what reaches the FSM.

comparisons.description: An entry sent by a server outside the recovered configuration neither is stored nor reaches the FSM.
